text.p: Sean O'Callaghan, an IRA guerrilla who became a top-level government informant, has been released from prison in Northern Ireland, British newspapers said.
O'Callaghan, 42, was released from Maghaberry Prison on Thursday after serving eight years of two life sentences for murder.

Credited with foiling an IRA plot to kill Prince Charles and his wife Princess Diana, he has been described by a senior Irish detective as "the most important intelligence agent in the history of the Irish state", the Sunday Times said.
O'Callaghan told the newspaper he wanted to tell the world about the Irish Republican Army, which he called "the seedbed of fascism" in its fight to drive Britain from Northern Ireland.
He predicted the IRA would declare a new ceasefire but said there was "not a chance" of it being genuine. "Republicans will murder many more people before this is over," he wrote.

After killing two members of the security forces in the 1970s, O'Callaghan became disillusioned with the IRA and turned against the organisation. He became an informant first for the Irish police and later for Britain's MI5 intelligence agency.
